reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline layer, the calculated high grain boundary energy implying possible decohesion, and the observation of cavitation-induced nanoporosity, all in the absence of segregation. However, the hypothesis extends these findings to claim that this cavitation directly causes toughness degradation and brittle failure, which is not explicitly demonstrated in the cited passages; the evidence links cavitation to superplasticity, not brittleness.
premises: Inverse Hall-Petch behavior and dynamic amorphization occur in single-phase CoCrFeMnNi under sliding in UHV, producing an ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer.
The ultra-nanocrystalline layer is associated with low friction and high wear resistance.
A calculated high-angle grain boundary energy of ~0.87 J/m² suggests a propensity for grain boundary decohesion even without segregation.
Cavitation-induced nanoporosity is observed in the highly deformed surface layer and is linked to superplasticity.
